chapters.title: Why you're still in it
chapters.teaser: The real reason your soul keeps saying 'let's see where it goes'.

chapters.title: What you actually want
chapters.teaser: Not what sounds chill. What you'd ask for if you weren't worried.

chapters.title: How you read mixed signals
chapters.teaser: Your decoding habit, and a better way to get information.

chapters.title: The talk, your way
chapters.teaser: How to ask 'what are we' in words that fit your soul.

chapters.title: Your line
chapters.teaser: The one thing you shouldn't keep accepting.

chapters.title: Either way, you're okay
chapters.teaser: What comes next, whatever answer you get.

text.why-you-stay: Eul Wood is the vine, and vines wrap around whatever is nearby. In a situationship you adapt to their rhythm: when they text, when they're free, what they're ready for. You're so good at making things easy that you can stay a long time without noticing you're always the one adjusting. You stay because connection matters to you, and some connection feels better than none. That's human. But ask yourself one gentle question: do I feel more secure since this started, or less? Your honest answer tells you more than any of their texts ever could.
text.what-you-want: You might honestly not know what you want, because you've been tuned to what they want for a while. Eul Wood is excellent at reading the room and slower at reading itself. So try this: imagine they offered you anything at all. What would you ask for? A title, consistency, being invited to things, a plan every week? Notice what comes up first, before you edit it down to something reasonable. That first answer is your want. It's allowed to be bigger than what you currently have, and it's allowed to be said out loud.
text.mixed-signals: When signals are mixed, you bend to fit them. They're distant, so you give space. They're warm, so you lean in. Eul Wood tends to read their signals as instructions for your own behaviour. The trouble is that your mood and your choices end up depending entirely on theirs. Try noticing your own signal instead. How do you feel after you see them? Lighter and settled, or anxious and checking your phone? That feeling is far clearer than anything they're sending, and it belongs completely to you. Start a quiet note on your phone and log that feeling after each meeting. After three or four entries, the pattern usually speaks for itself.
text.the-talk: Your talk can be gentle. That's your strength. But it needs one clear sentence in the middle, or you'll soften it into nothing. Try: I've really liked this, and I'd like to know if we're building toward something. Then add what you want, without apologising for wanting it. Eul Wood loves to offer an escape hatch at the end, the little no pressure though. Skip the escape hatch this time. Let it be a real question that deserves a real answer, and give them the silence they need to give you one.
text.your-line: Your line is being chosen. Eul Wood will put up with a lot of inconvenience, but you need to feel like a priority, not a backup plan for a quiet Thursday. Decide what that means in practice: plans made ahead of time, being introduced to people who matter to them, effort to see you that doesn't always come from your side. If that's consistently missing, that's your line. Stepping back doesn't make you dramatic or needy. It makes you someone who knows what shape fits your life, and keeps growing toward it.
text.either-way: Either way, you grow. If they want more, lovely, and this time make sure the adapting goes in both directions from the start. If they don't, you get your energy back to wind around things that hold you properly: friends, work, your own plans, maybe a new person who's actually ready. Eul Wood rebounds faster than anyone expects. You look delicate and you are incredibly hard to flatten. Give yourself a few soft days, then reach for the light again. You always find it. And next time, say what you want on the first or second date. It filters fast, and the right person finds it refreshing.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You make everything so easy for them, Eul.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Maybe too easy. When did they last adjust anything for you?

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your want is allowed to be bigger than this.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And drop the 'no pressure though!' Some pressure. A little.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Notice how you feel after you see them.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Lighter, or glued to your phone? That's your answer.

spring.intro: Spring-born Eul Wood is a vine in a season full of trellises. Wood doubled up in your birth month, so you connect easily and adapt beautifully. That's precisely why situationships find you. You can make almost anything work: their vague texts, their weekend-only availability, their line about being bad at labels. You wind yourself around the shape they offer and make it look pretty. The spring blind spot is too many supports and no commitment from any of them. You might even be keeping two or three half-things alive. Ask which one you'd actually choose if you had to. Adaptable is a gift. Infinitely flexible is a trap.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You've turned 'I'm bad at labels' into a cute garden feature. Stop decorating it.

summer.intro: In summer, Eul Wood blooms for an audience. Fire commanded your birth season and Wood feeds Fire, so your charm pours out: playful messages, great photos, the effortless fun person. In a situationship you've likely become the highlight reel. Light, easy, never heavy. The problem is that a bloom that never asks for water eventually droops. You may be hiding how much you want more because wanting seems unattractive. It isn't. Summer Eul's honesty move is small: let them see one serious thing. A real question, a real feeling. How they handle a little weight tells you whether this can hold your full bloom.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You don't have to be the fun one every time. Show one real feeling.

autumn.intro: Autumn Eul grew up under Metal's shears. That season put the controlling element in charge of your birth month, which made you skilled at reading rules nobody says out loud. In a situationship you probably know their moods better than they do. You adjust your texts, your timing, your availability. You avoid the talk because you can already feel the scissors. But constant adjusting makes you smaller, and you can't negotiate a relationship you're too pruned to show up in. The autumn gift is resilience: you recover from cuts better than most. Which means you can afford to ask. Whatever the answer, you'll grow.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You rewrote one text eleven times to sound casual. That's not casual, Eul.

winter.intro: Winter Eul is a bulb waiting under the frost. Water ruled your season and feeds your Wood, so your inner world is rich and patient. In a situationship you can wait a long time for a sign: a hint, a 'we should', a hand held in public once. You live on what might bloom. The winter blind spot is that bulbs can stay underground for years if nobody turns up the heat. You might be waiting for them to make it warm enough to come out and ask. You can bring your own warmth. Say the small true thing. Let it be cold for a minute. Then see what grows.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You're allowed to come up out of the frost and ask, Eul.

strength.strong: Eul, your chart wraps your vine in support, so you're socially confident and quietly tenacious. In a situationship that can turn into strategy: knowing exactly how to stay in their orbit, when to be fun, when to pull back. You're good at it, maybe too good. The blind spot is winning the game while losing the point. If you're managing the connection more than enjoying it, something's off. Drop the tactics for a week. Text when you want to, say what you mean. The right person responds to the real you, not the curated one.
strength.weak: With thin support in your chart, Eul, you grow by leaning on whoever's closest. In a situationship you might be leaning on someone who isn't holding you back. You adjust to their schedule, adopt their interests, wait for their move. The more you bend, the less of you they actually meet. The blind spot is believing flexibility will earn commitment. It usually earns more requests for flexibility. Plant something of your own: a plan you won't cancel, an opinion you'll keep. A vine with its own roots is easier to choose.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood means you push for growth and definition. In a situationship you might rush clarity, or picture a whole future before the other person has caught up to the present. Your drive is a good thing. Just give them room to answer at their own pace once you've asked. Ask once, clearly, then step back and let the answer come. Balance with a little Metal: clear boundaries, finished business, knowing when something needs pruning rather than more growth.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means starting things, including the talk, feels hard. You might let an undefined situation drift on and on simply because initiating anything feels heavy. Build momentum in small steps: decide what you want, write it down, choose a day to ask. Spend time outdoors and around green things. You don't need to grow everything at once. You only need one honest question, asked once, out loud.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire means big feelings, fast. In a situationship you might swing between excitement and frustration in the same evening, and want answers right now. Slow your pace a little. Pick a calm moment for the talk, not a heated one. Cool down with water: rest, quiet nights in, a walk before sending any big message. Your passion is attractive. Just don't let it make your decisions at midnight.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means expressing feelings and being seen can feel hard. You might keep this situationship low-key so that nobody, including you, has to admit it matters. Turn the light up a little. Let your feelings show in small ways. Be visible in your own life too: plans, friends, sunlight, music. The more you shine for yourself, the easier the honest question becomes when you finally ask it.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth means you wait, stay steady, and stay put, sometimes for too long. In a situationship you may tolerate a lack of definition because change feels disruptive and messy. Bring in a bit of movement: pick a day by which you'll have the talk, and keep it. Let some Wood in, growth and fresh starts. Stable doesn't have to mean stuck, and patient doesn't have to mean silent.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means stability is hard to find, and an undefined relationship can make you feel even more unsteady than usual. Ground yourself first: routines, regular meals, a dependable circle of friends. Then have the talk from a steady place, not a shaky one. You'll think more clearly and ask more clearly when your own ground is solid under your feet, whatever the answer turns out to be.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal means you want clarity and might cut too fast to get it. In a situationship you may issue ultimatums or go cold the moment things feel vague. Your boundaries are strong, which is good. Soften the delivery: ask with curiosity first, decide second. Water helps here: rest, reflection, letting a feeling be felt before you act on it.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are hard. In a situationship you may accept less than you want and keep telling yourself it's fine. Practise clear edges: decide your line and write it down somewhere you'll see it. Say no to plans that don't work for you. White and silver, decluttering, finishing things all support you. A boundary isn't harsh. It's honesty about what you need.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water means overthinking and very deep feeling. In a situationship you might analyse every message and drown in what-ifs that never happen. Your intuition is valuable, but it needs a shore to land on. Earth helps: routines, physical activity, friends who ground you. Put a limit on the analysis. Ask the question instead of guessing the answer.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means reflection and rest get skipped. You might keep the situationship busy and fun so you never have to stop and think about what it actually is. Make space for quiet: a journal, a slow evening, a moment alone to ask yourself what you really want here. Clarity starts inside you before it's ever spoken to them, and it's worth the quiet.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: you've planned your future together. They haven't planned Saturday.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: That growing energy is lovely. Point it at what you want, not only at them.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: one great date and you're naming the dog. Breathe.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is magnetic. Let them match it before you double it.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth: you've waited so patiently you've basically become their furniture.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness is a gift. It's fair to ask for steadiness back.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal: you've drafted an ultimatum. Maybe try a question first.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your clarity is strength. Soften the delivery and it lands beautifully.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you analysed one 'haha' with three friends and a tarot app.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your sensitivity notices so much. Check the signals against actual actions too.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood can make it hard to picture what you want. Try imagining it.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: No Wood, no vision. You're seeing where it goes without looking anywhere.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can make it hard to show interest. A little warmth helps.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: No Fire. They genuinely cannot tell if you like them. Neither can I.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth makes it easy to drift. Choose one thing you're sure about.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth, no ground. You change your mind about them every other day.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal can blur your line. You can decide what you won't accept.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal means no line. You'll accept 'wyd' at midnight forever.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can make feelings hard to say. Try writing them first.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: No Water. You'd rather move countries than say 'I like you.'

gap-wood.title: The tree, the vine and the maybe
gap-wood.text: You and a Gap Wood can talk all day and still be standing in two different conversations. You send the voice note, the meme, the screenshot of a playlist called 'songs for no reason'. Gap replies 'ha' or 'ok' and you spend twenty minutes deciding whether that was cold. Usually it was just short. Gap texts like a person confirming a delivery. The drift in this pair comes from your side as much as theirs. When Gap pushes for something concrete, you agree warmly in the moment and then quietly do things your own way, and the plan stays a soft 'maybe Saturday'. To a Gap, maybe is not an answer, and it starts to look like you're keeping a door open behind you. The signal you send is lightness. It reads as charming and also as not quite in. For the talk, give Gap the straight line first and the softness second. Something like: I want this to be a real relationship. I also want it to stay fun. Is that where you are too? Gap respects a clear question more than anything you could hint at. You don't need to be less playful. You just need one sentence that doesn't wriggle.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul's voice notes and Gap's 'ok' are both affection. Different dialects.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: One of you needs to stop wriggling. The other needs more than one word.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Clear question first, cat sticker second.

eul-wood.title: Two vines and nobody decides
eul-wood.text: Two Eul Woods in a situationship are a delight to be around and almost impossible to pin down. You text all day. Voice notes on the bus, stickers, a link to a ceramics class you'll definitely take together someday, 'omg same' forty times a week. From the outside, you look like a couple. From the inside, nobody has said it, because nobody wants to be the one who makes it heavy. The drift for two vines is the soft maybe. Where are we going Saturday? Wherever you want. Should we go to the wedding together? Maybe, we'll see. Both of you wait for the other to decide, and both of you are very good at being agreeable while waiting. Watch the jealousy, too. You both know exactly how charming the other is with everyone else, and a story view from someone new can turn into a quiet comparison. The talk for this pair has one rule: do it face to face, not in the chat. The chat is where big topics go to become memes. Pick a calm afternoon and say: I don't want to keep floating. I want us to be a real couple. One of you has to be the one who decides. It might as well be you.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Two vines, endless voice notes. The sweetest group chat of two.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And zero decisions. 'Wherever you want' is not a plan.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Big talk face to face. The chat turns everything into stickers.

byeong-fire.title: Bloom season at the far end of the table
byeong-fire.text: Being near a Byeong Fire is bloom season. Everything feels warmer, the city looks better, and the heart emojis come in by the dozen. Byeong calls instead of texting and laughs loudly enough that the people at the next table smile too. You turn towards that light without trying. The drift begins at the edges. Byeong is the centre of every room, and in a situationship there's no rule that says you get the seat next to them. You end up at the far end of the table at Byeong's birthday drinks, introduced as 'this is Eul!' with nothing after it. So you find subtle ways to be seen: a story posted at the right moment, a slightly cooler reply, a mention of someone else who asked you out. Byeong tends to read that as games. Byeong also forgets plans that you remembered word for word. For the talk, you need plain words more than strategy. Byeong responds to warmth and directness, not to puzzles: I really like you, and I want to be more than one of the people around you. Are you in this with me? Say 'I miss you' plainly, too. Flowers don't have to be subtle.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong, the flower is turning towards you. Look down once in a while.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Eul, the strategic story post is not a conversation.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Say 'I miss you' plainly. Both of you.

jeong-fire.title: Love letters disguised as texts
jeong-fire.text: With a Jeong Fire, everything feels like candlelight: low, warm, slightly cinematic. Your messages are long and full of feeling. You both read between the lines like it's a sport, and you're both very good at it. That's precisely why this situationship can go a long time without anyone saying what it is. The drift is two soft people being careful. You go vague when something bothers you; Jeong goes quiet. You assume Jeong's silence is a mood. Jeong may assume your vagueness is distance. Add your wide social life, the brunches, the group trips, the housewarming where you stayed until 2, and Jeong can start to feel like one candle among many lamps. You might notice a little possessiveness in the questions about who was there. That's usually the flame asking for focus, not trying to control you. Late at night, you can both spiral, amplifying each other's worries over text. For the talk, choose daylight and a quiet place, and give Jeong focus: I want this to be just us. I'd like to call it a relationship. Would you? Then agree on a code word for 'I'm actually upset', so feelings stop hiding behind emojis.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You two write love letters disguised as texts. Gorgeous.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And neither of you has said the actual thing. Code word, please.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Jeong, ask for focus. Eul, give it out loud.

mu-earth.title: Climbing the mountain the clever way
mu-earth.text: A Mu Earth is the mountain you've decided to climb, and you're doing it the way vines do: around, gently, with a lot of charm. You send the funny reel, the 'thinking of you', the photo of a dog in a raincoat. Mu replies three hours later with 'ha. nice.' and you wonder if you're climbing a mountain or a wall. Here's the translation: Mu's 'ok' is warm. It's just warmth delivered at mountain speed. The drift in this pair happens when you start working around Mu instead of talking to them. If Mu won't commit to the weekend, you try charm, then hints, then a quiet manoeuvre, like inviting their best friend so Mu has to come. Mu notices manoeuvres, and Mu hardens when it feels handled. You might also start to find Mu a bit slow, and Mu might find your social calendar a bit much. For the talk, skip the clever route and go straight up: I like you, and I want this to be a real relationship. What do you think? Then let the silence sit. Mu thinks before answering. A slow answer from a mountain is usually a considered one.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu, your 'ok' is warm. Eul just can't hear it from down here.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Eul, inviting their best friend so they have to come? Cute. Also sneaky.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Straight up the mountain. No clever route.

gi-earth.title: Who is feeding whom in this garden
gi-earth.text: A Gi Earth is the soil every vine dreams of: warm, generous, attentive. Gi remembers your exam date, brings you soup when you have a cold, asks if you got home safe when you forgot to say. In a situationship, that care can feel like a relationship without anyone having to say so. And that's the drift. You grow into the space Gi makes, and Gi keeps making more. You send the fun things, memes, playlists, a photo of a cake you saw. Gi sends practical questions, like when you're free next week or whether you still want to go to their cousin's thing. You answer the meme and skip the question. To Gi, that's a small hole in the garden. Gi tends to worry quietly, and you tend to brush worries off as overthinking. Over weeks, Gi can start to feel used and you can start to feel nagged, and neither of you says a word. For the talk, answer the logistics first. That's how Gi feels chosen. Then ask: You give me so much. I want to give back properly and be in a real relationship. What do you need from me? Listen to the whole answer. Gi rarely asks for much, so whatever they name matters.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi, you're allowed to have needs in this garden too.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Eul, answer the practical question before the meme. Every time.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Equal is a fair thing to ask for.

gyeong-metal.title: The blade asks, the vine sends a frog
gyeong-metal.text: 乙 and 庚 are a heavenly combination, the vine that wraps the blade, and you can feel the pull. A Gyeong Metal is everything you're not: blunt, decisive, a bit intimidating, and weirdly protective. When they text 'Where are you.' with a full stop, part of you finds it thrilling. The other part wants to send a sticker and a voice note about a cat you saw. Which you do. That's the drift in one exchange. Gyeong asks a straight question and you answer sideways. When Gyeong gets frustrated, the words get sharper, and when you're hurt, you get slipperier, agreeing in the moment and then quietly doing your own thing. The situationship can feel intense and still undefined, because one of you is too direct to hint and the other too gentle to be direct. Gyeong's signal is bluntness, which isn't coldness. Yours is charm, which isn't commitment. For the talk, give Gyeong the straight answer first and the cat second: I want us to be together. That's my answer. What's yours? You don't lose any softness by being clear. You gain a Gyeong who knows where to stand.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: 乙庚 is a real pull. Steel and vine, oddly perfect.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Eul, answer 'where are you' with an address. Then the frog.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gyeong, wait ten minutes. Then be warm and clear.

sin-metal.title: Read receipts and the pruning shears
sin-metal.text: A Sin Metal is beautiful, precise, and a little bit scary to text. You write a message, delete it, write it again, and wait. Sin does exactly the same on the other side. Read receipts become a sport neither of you enjoys. The drift in this situationship tends to begin with a small comment. Sin says something precise about your outfit, your friend, the way you never book restaurants in advance, and to Sin it's helpful pruning. To you, it lands as 'not quite enough'. So you adapt. You dress a bit more like Sin would, you say yes to plans you're not sure about, you become very agreeable. Sin can read that agreeableness as having no backbone, which is the opposite of what you intended. Then somebody goes a little cold, nobody names it, and a week passes. Your signal is adaptability, which can look like you have no opinion about this. For the talk, show Sin your opinion. That's the attractive part: I like you a lot, and I want this to be a relationship. I also need it to feel kind. Can we do both? Someone has to say 'I miss you' first. Let it be you, and let it be plain.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You both reread every text. Imagine just sending one.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Sin, that 'small note' was a pruning. Put the scissors down.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul, have an opinion. It's the attractive part.

im-water.title: Fast growth, no map
im-water.text: An Im Water is a river, and you're the vine that grows fastest near it. Everything feels alive: last-minute trips, memes at 2 a.m., a plan to learn surfing that you both half believe. You adapt to Im's current easily, maybe too easily. The drift in this pair is so pleasant it doesn't feel like drifting. Both of you love freedom, so nobody brings up the boring question of what this is. It's always next month. Then Im disappears into a project, a new idea, a trip with friends, and goes dark for a day or three. You find it lonely and don't say so, because saying so feels uncool. Instead you overthink, check whether Im watched your story, and draft messages you don't send. Your signal is easygoing. Im can read that as you being fine with total looseness. For the talk, ask instead of overthinking. You don't need a big conversation. You need one honest question: I love the freedom we have. I'd also like us to be a real couple. Is that something you'd want? Ask during one of Im's good, chatty moods. And name what you need in plain words, like a small daily check-in, so you stop guessing.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: River and vine. Fast growth, lots of fun, no map.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Im, a two-word check-in. You can manage two words.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul, ask instead of overthinking. You're allowed.

gye-water.title: The exhibition that has been 'soon' since July
gye-water.text: A Gye Water is morning dew to you: quiet, intuitive, deeply kind. You send songs back and forth. You have a shared playlist with a name only the two of you understand. You can talk until 3 a.m. about nothing and feel completely understood. And still, no one has said what this is. The drift here is gentleness. Neither of you likes conflict, so anything uncomfortable gets rained on and wished away. When Gye goes moody or withdrawn, you try to cheer them up with memes and plans, and if it doesn't work, you quietly feel rejected and go soft and vague yourself. Plans dissolve because neither of you sets a direction: 'we should go to that exhibition' has been on the list since summer. Your signal is brightness, which to Gye can feel like pressure to be okay. Gye's signal is withdrawal, which is usually about weather inside Gye, not about you. For the talk, say it clearly first and then add the song: I want us to be together for real, not just in our playlist. Do you? Bring a practical question too, like what you're doing for the holidays. Dew needs something to settle on.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Shared playlist, 3 a.m. talks. You two are a soft little film.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: That exhibition has been 'soon' since July. Pick a date.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sentence first, song second.
